claim: CMS's remote patient monitoring page, last modified May 13, 2026.
quote: Page Last Modified: 05/13/2026 02:16 PM

claim: "Remote patient monitoring allows a patient to collect their own health data, like blood pressure, weight, and glucose levels, using a connected medical device that automatically transmits the data to their health care provider."
quote: Remote patient monitoring allows a patient to collect their own health data, like blood pressure, weight, and glucose levels, using a connected medical device that automatically transmits the data to their health care provider.

claim: The provider then uses that data "to treat or manage (remotely monitor) the patient's condition."
quote: The provider then uses this data to treat or manage (remotely monitor) the patient’s condition.

claim: CMS names connected blood pressure cuffs, weight scales and pulse oximeters as example devices.
quote: Examples of these devices include connected blood pressure cuffs, weight scales, and pulse oximeters.

claim: "Medicare broadly covers remote patient monitoring (sometimes called remote physiologic monitoring) for the collection of any type of physiologic data using a wide range of devices, for chronic and acute conditions."
quote: Medicare broadly covers remote patient monitoring (sometimes called remote physiologic monitoring) for the collection of any type of physiologic data using a wide range of devices, for chronic and acute conditions.

claim: The patient has "a chronic or acute condition that requires monitoring".
quote: Have a chronic or acute condition that requires monitoring

claim: In CMS's example, the provider decides the service is medically necessary.
quote: The patient’s provider determines that the remote patient monitoring is medically necessary to treat his hypertension and the patient consents to getting it.

claim: An internet-connected device that "Meets that FDA's definition of a medical device and digitally uploads data".
quote: Meets that FDA’s definition of a medical device and digitally uploads data

claim: A device that "Collects and transmits health data at least 2 days every 30 days".
quote: Collects and transmits health data at least 2 days every 30 days

claim: The device-supply component counts readings: "the collection and transmission of at least 2 readings every 30 days".
quote: The internet-connected device, including the collection and transmission of at least 2 readings every 30 days, ensure that you get the appropriate health information.

claim: Education and setup, so the patient uses the device appropriately and collects accurate data.
quote: Education about how to use the device and transmit the health data helps ensure that patients use the device appropriately to collect accurate data.

claim: Treatment and management, the provider reviewing the data and using it to manage the patient's condition.
quote: Treatment management ensures that you review the health data and use it to manage the patient’s condition.

claim: CMS pays for each of the three components separately, at "the same rate, regardless of the type of device the patient uses or the health data they collect".
quote: We pay for each of the 3 main components separately and pay the same rate, regardless of the type of device the patient uses or the health data they collect.

claim: CMS doesn't "require that physicians or other qualified health care providers order the services or that the information of the ordering provider be included on the claim."
quote: We don’t require that physicians or other qualified health care providers order the services or that the information of the ordering provider be included on the claim.

claim: The page names a general set of procedure codes but no codes or amounts.
quote: Bill Medicare for remote patient monitoring services using a general set of procedure codes, which represent different components of the monitoring.

claim: It has covered remote patient monitoring since 2018, and use has grown every year.
quote: Medicare started covering remote patient monitoring starting in 2018. Since that time, the number of patients getting remote patient monitoring has increased significantly each year.

claim: "Many patients don't get education or help with device setup." It tells providers to deliver all three components.
quote: When providing for and billing the services, be sure you provide all 3 main components. Many patients don’t get education or help with device setup.

claim: The guidance says section 520(o)(1)(B) of the FD&C Act makes software intended "for maintaining or encouraging a healthy lifestyle and is unrelated to the diagnosis, cure, mitigation, prevention, or treatment of a disease or condition" not a device.
quote: Section 520(o)(1)(B) of the FD&C Act, states that software that is intended "for maintaining or encouraging a healthy lifestyle and is unrelated to the diagnosis, cure, mitigation, prevention, or treatment of a disease or condition" is not a device under section 201(h) of the FD&C Act.

claim: The FTC's tool asks whether you are "developing, offering, or operating an app on behalf of a HIPAA covered entity (such as a hospital, doctor's office, health insurer, or health plan's wellness program)".
quote: Are you developing, offering, or operating an app on behalf of a HIPAA covered entity (such as a hospital, doctor’s office, health insurer, or health plan’s wellness program)?

claim: ...and answers that if so, "You likely are a HIPAA business associate".
quote: You likely are a HIPAA business associate , and therefore subject to the HIPAA Security Rule and specific provisions of the HIPAA Privacy and Breach Notification Rules

claim: HIPAA's definitions make a business associate a person who, on behalf of a covered entity, "creates, receives, maintains, or transmits protected health information".
quote: creates, receives, maintains, or transmits protected health information for a function or activity regulated by this subchapter

claim: CMS says a covered entity that engages a business associate "must have a written business associate contract or other arrangement".
quote: the covered entity must have a written business associate contract or other arrangement with the business associate

claim: CMS's telehealth section lists a remote patient monitoring page and no remote therapeutic monitoring page.
quote: Telehealth List of Telehealth Services Requests for Additions CMS Review Criteria Useful Links Changes and Deletion of Services Remote Patient Monitoring
